subject: Exploring GitHub integration for OSS CI — demo scheduling
messages:
From: Evan Turner <evan@openforge.dev>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Interest: GitHub integration for our OSS CI pipeline

Hi Marissa,

We signed up via the website and selected a demo slot, but didn't get a confirmation. We're evaluating tools to power a lightweight OSS CI that can run on contributors' forks without leaking secrets. Primary questions: do you support GitHub Apps with limited repo access, can Redwood run in a self-hosted runner, and how does webhook auth work for forks?

A bit about us: OpenForge builds buildkite-like tooling for open-source projects; we manage builds for ~150 repos. Happy to share more context on the call.

Thanks,
Evan Turner
Head of Integrations
OpenForge
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Turner <evan@openforge.dev>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interest: GitHub integration for our OSS CI pipeline

Hi Evan — thanks for signing up and for the context. I'm Marissa on the SDR team and I own intake for OSS leads. Quick answers up front: yes, we support GitHub Apps with scoped permissions; Redwood Private can run in customer VPCs and we have integrations patterns for runner-based workflows; webhooks can be validated via HMAC and we offer forward-proxy patterns for forked PRs.

To make the demo useful, could you confirm: 1) whether OpenForge wants hosted Redwood or Private (VPC/on-prem) for this workload, 2) an example repo (public is fine) we can hook into for a short live demo, and 3) preferred timezone for scheduling (so we avoid repeating last-minute conflicts).

Proposed windows (PDT):
- Tue Oct 6: 10:00–11:00 or 15:00–15:30
- Wed Oct 7: 09:00–09:45 or 14:00–14:45

Looping in Ben (solutions engineer) to cover the platform architecture and a technical checklist. If you can share a short description of your runner model and whether secrets are injected at runtime, Ben will tailor the demo.

Best,
Marissa Cole
SDR, Redwood Inference
From: Evan Turner <evan@openforge.dev>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: OpenForge Integrations <integrations@openforge.dev>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interest: GitHub integration for our OSS CI pipeline

Hi Marissa — thanks for the quick reply. We expect to use Redwood Private inside our AWS account (VPC) because of data residency and secret handling. Example repo: https://github.com/openforge/example-runner. Our runners are ephemeral AWS Fargate tasks; secrets are injected via an internal secrets service at runtime, not stored in the repo.

Any of the Wed Oct 7 slots work best for us (prefer morning PDT). Please go ahead and schedule with Ben if he's available.

—Evan

Thanks Evan — Ben here from Solutions. Wed Oct 7 at 09:00 PDT works for me. I'll prepare a short 25-minute technical demo + 15-minute Q&A focused on: GitHub App permissions, runner auth patterns for forks, KV cache and secrets handling when running in a customer VPC, and a suggested rollout plan for OSS repos.

Attaching a short checklist and proposed agenda to help you prep. If you have any specific API keys or logs you'd like me to review in advance, please send them over (secure link preferred).

Agenda (attached):
- 0–5m: intros & success criteria
- 5–20m: live walkthrough on openforge/example-runner
- 20–35m: architecture deep-dive (VPC, auth, secrets)
- 35–45m: next steps & mutual action items

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
